title: Kabar Baik, Kabar Buruk — Kenapa Bumi Tidak Jatuh?
question: Kenapa Bumi tidak jatuh — dan bisakah jawaban sainsnya hidup dalam format dialog Kabar Baik, Kabar Buruk gaya petir?
audience: Penonton Shorts vertikal di ponsel, menonton sering tanpa suara; seluruh gag harus terbaca dari huruf dan gambar.
promise: Kabar baiknya Bumi tidak akan jatuh ke bawah karena di luar angkasa tidak ada 'bawah'; kabar buruknya Bumi sebenarnya jatuh terus ke arah Matahari — tetapi selalu meleset, dan itulah orbit.

voice.name: Dua register Piper TTS lokal (id_ID-news_tts-medium): A dinaikkan x1.07 dan lebih cepat, B diturunkan x0.86 dan lebih lambat — pola dua suara episode orisinal yang tayang (15 Nov 2026).
voice.model: Piper TTS (rhasspy) id_ID-news_tts-medium, length-scale A 0.95 / B 1.05, pitch-shift ffmpeg dengan durasi dipulihkan
voice.note: PENYIMPANGAN TERCATAT: episode uji Keran memakai dua desain OmniVoice via VoiceStudio, tetapi di VM ini generasi OmniVoice melewati batas komputasi 600 detik dua kali (job gugur) — satu baris 8 kata pun tidak selesai. Piper adalah mesin episode orisinal yang LOLOS dan tayang. Dialog digabung jadi satu take dengan jeda antarbaris (assemble.py); voice.mjs menyelaraskan kata-katanya: 85% selaras, kata yang perlu didengar Icul: nggak, ke pusat, Terus-terusan, tiga puluh kilometer. Tidak ada yang mendengarkan take ini.

look.mood: Panggung petir-guntur di bawah langit luar angkasa: dinding dan lantai grafit, Matahari amber menyala di tengah, elips orbit berputus-putus ungu, Bumi biru-hijau, dua tokoh siluet hitam bertepi cahaya ungu. Amber = tokoh A, Matahari dan kabar baik; ungu = tokoh B dan orbit.

music.note: Bed yang sama dengan episode Keran: 86 BPM, naik halus, tanpa melodi utama, jadi dialog memimpin.

facts.claim: Di luar angkasa tidak ada arah 'bawah' yang mutlak; bagi benda di Bumi, 'bawah' adalah arah ke pusat Bumi, ke situlah gravitasi Bumi menariknya.
facts.source: Fisika dasar gravitasi: arah jatuh ditentukan oleh pusat massa penarik (buku teks fisika umum).

facts.claim: Bumi terus-menerus jatuh ke arah Matahari karena gravitasi Matahari, tetapi gerak menyampingnya membuat jatuh itu selalu meleset; gabungan keduanya adalah orbit.
facts.source: Mekanika orbit Newton (gagasan meriam Newton): orbit adalah jatuh bebas yang terus-menerus meleset dari penariknya.

facts.claim: Kecepatan orbit Bumi mengelilingi Matahari rata-rata sekitar 29,8 kilometer per detik, dibulatkan menjadi tiga puluh kilometer per detik.
facts.source: NASA Earth Facts: kecepatan orbit Bumi 29,78 km/detik.

acts.title: Pembuka
acts.goal: Perkenalkan diorama luar angkasa di panggung petir dan kalimat pembuka formatnya; B memilih kabar baik dulu.

acts.title: Kabar Baik
acts.goal: Kabar baik disampaikan dengan kejadian visualnya: panah 'bawah' dicoret, apel jatuh ke pusat Bumi; B lega dan meminta kabar buruknya.

acts.title: Kabar Buruk
acts.goal: Putarannya: Bumi ternyata jatuh terus ke arah Matahari; B panik; A menjelaskan gerak menyamping 30 km/detik yang membuat jatuhnya selalu meleset — itulah orbit.

acts.title: Kartu Penutup
acts.goal: Satu kalimat penutup jenaka di atas panggung yang meredup, Bumi tetap berputar di orbitnya.

shots.voice: Bro, aku punya kabar baik dan kabar buruk.
shots.caption: Bro, aku punya kabar baik dan *kabar buruk*.
shots.teaches: The format's opening line, and the set: a space diorama on the petir stage — the Sun at centre, Earth resting at the left of its dashed orbit, the two figures below.
shots.screen: Wide on the petir stage at night. Graphite wall and floor, starfield, the Sun glowing amber at centre (540,690), a dashed violet orbit ellipse around it, Earth blue-green at the ellipse's left point (180,690). A at x 400 faces right, B at x 880 with folded arms. A's line in metal type, top third, amber chip.
shots.motion: Slow push-in (z 1.0 to 1.08). Earth bobs gently; the Sun's rays turn very slowly. A gestures as he speaks; B does not move.
shots.carries: The Sun, the orbit ellipse and Earth stay for the whole film; the figures stay on the floor line.
shots.transition: Cut on B's reply; the camera glides toward B.
shots.sound: Music bed under; the line sits on the voice.
shots.check: Frame 0 is a finished picture: both figures, Sun, Earth, orbit and the first words readable; nothing clipped.

frames.note: Frame 0: the diorama complete, A turns to B.

draw.text:
Bro, aku punya kabar baik
dan kabar buruk.

frames.note: A gestures toward B; Earth bobs at the left.
Held wide; the opening line is complete.

shots.caption: Kabar baiknya *dulu* deh.
shots.teaches: B chooses the good news first — the format's ritual beat.
shots.screen: Closer two-shot favouring B (camera glides right, z 1.16). B unfolds one arm and lifts a palm. His line in metal type with the violet chip. The diorama glows behind them.
shots.motion: B unfolds one arm and lifts a palm, unhurried, as he chooses; A settles into listening and does not move again.
shots.carries: The diorama stays; Earth's gentle bob continues behind them.
shots.transition: Cut to the good news; the camera pushes toward Earth.
shots.sound: Music bed under; the line sits on the voice.
shots.check: B's palm reads clearly; both figures fully in frame.

frames.note: B lifts a palm: the good news first, please.
Held two-shot; A listens, B palm still up.
The line complete; the camera settles.

shots.voice: Kabar baiknya: Bumi nggak akan jatuh ke bawah.
shots.caption: Kabar baiknya: Bumi nggak akan jatuh ke *bawah*.
shots.teaches: The good news itself: Earth will not fall 'down'.
shots.screen: Camera pushes to Earth (z 1.45, centred 300,690). Under Earth a big amber down-arrow draws itself as A speaks — the fall everybody imagines — and hangs there, waiting to be denied.
shots.motion: The camera push runs the shot's first third; the down-arrow draws itself under Earth through the second half of the line.
shots.carries: Earth enlarged centre-left; the drawn arrow carries into the next shot to be crossed out.
shots.transition: No cut in the argument: the same push holds into the denial.
shots.sound: Music bed under; the line sits on the voice.
shots.check: The arrow's direction is unambiguous and it is large enough to read at phone size.

frames.note: Push-in on Earth; A begins the good news.

draw.text:
Bumi nggak akan jatuh
ke bawah.

frames.note: The amber down-arrow draws under Earth.
The arrow complete, hanging under Earth.

shots.voice: Di luar angkasa nggak ada 'bawah' — semua benda justru ditarik ke pusat Bumi.
shots.caption: Di luar angkasa nggak ada *'bawah'* — semua benda ditarik ke *pusat Bumi*.
shots.teaches: The first fact: there is no absolute 'down' in space; for things on Earth, 'down' is toward Earth's centre, where its gravity pulls.
shots.screen: The same macro on Earth. The amber arrow is crossed out in violet as 'nggak ada bawah' lands. A tiny figure stands on Earth's top; an apple drops from beside him along a curved arrow into the planet, ending at a bright centre dot that lights.
shots.motion: The cross strikes at the first clause; the apple falls through the second clause and the centre dot lights exactly on 'pusat Bumi'.
shots.carries: Earth stays enlarged; the lit centre dot stays for the rest of the film.
shots.transition: Cut wide again on B's reply.
shots.sound: Music bed under; a soft tick as the cross strikes; a tiny pop when the centre dot lights.
shots.check: The crossed arrow and the apple's path to the centre both read at phone size; no text over the bright Sun.

frames.note: The cross strikes through the down-arrow.
The apple falls from the surface figure.
The apple nears the centre; the dot brightens.
The centre dot lights inside Earth.

draw.text:
semua benda ditarik
ke pusat Bumi.

shots.voice: Wah, aman dong! Terus kabar buruknya?
shots.caption: Wah, aman dong! Terus, *kabar buruknya*?
shots.teaches: B relaxes — and asks for the bad news, the format's hinge.
shots.screen: Wide again (z 1.05). Earth rests at the left of the orbit; B, delighted, points toward A as he asks. A turns back toward the diorama.
shots.motion: B points at the line's turn toward the question; A turns from B back to the diorama as the question lands.
shots.carries: The diorama resets: Earth back at the left point, the crossed arrow gone.
shots.transition: Cut closer on A and Earth for the bad news.
shots.sound: Music bed under; the line sits on the voice.
shots.check: B's point reads; the question lands before the cut.

frames.note: Wide again; B delighted by the good news.
B points at A: and the bad news is?
Held; A turns back to the diorama.

shots.voice: Kabar buruknya… Bumi lagi jatuh. Terus-terusan. Ke arah Matahari.
shots.caption: Kabar buruknya… Bumi lagi *jatuh*. Ke arah *Matahari*.
shots.teaches: The turn, and the second fact's first half: Earth really is falling, continuously, toward the Sun, pulled by the Sun's gravity.
shots.screen: Closer (z 1.22, centred on the diorama). As A speaks, Earth leaves the ellipse's left point and slides right toward the Sun along a dashed amber fall-arrow; the Sun's glow grows as Earth nears it.
shots.motion: Earth's slide starts on the word 'jatuh' and keeps creeping through 'terus-terusan'; the fall-arrow's dashes draw ahead of it toward the Sun.
shots.carries: Earth mid-fall, between the ellipse and the Sun; it does not stop falling for the rest of the film.
shots.transition: Cut to B's panic, Earth still creeping.
shots.sound: Music bed under, ridden down a touch; a low whoosh under the slide.
shots.check: Earth's motion direction is unambiguous: toward the Sun, not downward.

frames.note: A delivers it flat; Earth still at the left.
Earth slides toward the Sun on the arrow.
Earth nearer the Sun, still falling inward.

shots.voice: Hah?! Kita bakal nabrak Matahari, dong?!
shots.caption: Hah?! Kita bakal *nabrak* Matahari, dong?!
shots.teaches: B's panic — the question the explanation has to answer.
shots.screen: Two-shot favouring B. Both figures throw their hands up; a single violet-white lightning flash cracks behind the stage as B shouts. Earth hangs close to the Sun, trembling.
shots.motion: Hands go up exactly on 'Hah?!'; one lightning flash cracks at the shot's start; Earth trembles in place near the Sun throughout.
shots.carries: Earth close to the Sun, still falling — the danger is real until A answers.
shots.transition: Cut wide for the explanation; Earth veers.
shots.sound: A thunder tick under the flash; the line sits on the voice.
shots.check: The panic reads on mute; the flash is one beat, not a strobe.

frames.note: Hands up; the lightning flash cracks.
B shouts; Earth trembles beside the Sun.
Held panic; the flash has faded out.

shots.voice: Tenang. Bumi juga melesat menyamping, tiga puluh kilometer per detik.
shots.caption: Tenang. Bumi juga melesat *menyamping*, *tiga puluh kilometer per detik*.
shots.teaches: The rescue's mechanism and the number: Earth also moves sideways at about thirty kilometres a second.
shots.screen: Wide (z 1.0). A raises an open palm — calm. Earth veers up and past the Sun, a violet speed-arrow tangent at its nose, motion lines trailing; B's arms slowly come down as he listens.
shots.motion: The veer lands on the word 'menyamping'; Earth passes above the Sun through the number and settles toward the ellipse's top point.
shots.carries: Earth above the Sun, aimed along the ellipse; the fall-arrow is gone, replaced by the speed-arrow.
shots.transition: No cut: the same wide holds as Earth settles onto the ellipse.
shots.sound: Music bed under; a whoosh rides the veer and fades as Earth settles.
shots.check: The sideways direction reads against the earlier fall: across, not down and not in.

frames.note: A, palm open: calm. Earth begins to veer.
Earth swings past above the Sun, fast.
Earth settles toward the ellipse's top.

shots.voice: Jadi jatuhnya selalu meleset — dan memutar. Itulah orbit.
shots.caption: Jadi jatuhnya selalu *meleset* — dan memutar. Itulah *orbit*.
shots.teaches: The payoff and the term: falling plus forever missing, repeated, is an orbit — said and shown at the same moment.
shots.screen: The same wide. Earth settles onto the dashed ellipse, which lights up violet as Earth completes the loop and keeps going. A lowers his palm; B, arms down now, watches it go around.
shots.motion: The ellipse lights progressively as Earth travels it; the loop completes exactly on the word 'orbit' and Earth does not stop.
shots.carries: Earth on its lit orbit, looping for the rest of the film; the film's question is answered.
shots.transition: No cut: the same wide holds into the silent recap beat.
shots.sound: Music bed under; a shimmer rises as the ellipse lights up fully.
shots.check: The loop reads as a loop: Earth passes the Sun and comes around; 'orbit' is said and shown together.

frames.note: Earth settles onto the dashed ellipse.
Half the loop travelled; the ellipse lighting.
Three-quarter loop done; the ellipse nearly lit.
The loop complete and lit: 'Itulah orbit.'

shots.caption: …dan putaran itu *tidak pernah berhenti*.
shots.teaches: The recap in one frame: Earth falls forever, misses forever, and the loop — the orbit — never stops.
shots.screen: The same wide, no voices. Earth keeps looping on the lit ellipse; the two figures watch it go around, heads turning with it. The note line letters in, lower and quieter, over the stage.
shots.motion: Earth completes another half loop while both heads track it; the note types in at 0.85 s and holds to the end of the shot.
shots.carries: Earth looping into the end card; the stage begins to dim.
shots.transition: The stage dims under the end card; no cut.
shots.sound: Music only, resolving; a soft shimmer as the note lands.
shots.check: The note is readable for at least two seconds; Earth visibly still moving.

frames.note: Silent wide; Earth looping, heads tracking.
The recap note letters in over the stage.
Held recap; the dim begins at the edges.

shots.caption: Jatuh terus, meleset terus — itulah *orbit*.
shots.teaches: The closing line of the format, as a poster over the dimming stage: the whole science in one joke-shaped sentence.
shots.screen: The stage dims to near-night; Earth still loops on its lit ellipse behind the card. Centre frame, the closing line in metal type: 'Jatuh terus, meleset terus — itulah orbit.' with 'orbit' in amber; above it small, the series title 'KABAR BAIK, KABAR BURUK'.
shots.motion: The line types in over the first 1.2 s; a slow push (z 1.0 to 1.05) for the rest; Earth keeps looping behind the card to the last frame.
shots.carries: The last frame is the poster; nothing follows it in this film.
shots.transition: The film ends on this held poster frame.
shots.sound: Music resolves and fades under the card.
shots.check: Poster readable for at least two seconds; text exact; Earth still moving behind the card.

frames.note: Dim stage; the line beginning to type in.

The poster held: line complete, Earth looping.
